subject: geography
title: Magma Genesis & Volcanic Hazards
welcome_lead: Link magma chemistry to eruption style.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on magma genesis, VEI and Iceland 2010 case study.

concepts.def: Low silica (<52 percent), low viscosity, effusive eruptions; e.g. Hawaii.
Intermediate silica (52-63 percent), explosive composite cones; e.g. Mt Fuji.
High silica (>63 percent), highly viscous, most explosive; e.g. Yellowstone.
Volcanic Explosivity Index (0-8); each step is 10x more explosive.
Hot gas + ash + rock flowing at up to 700 km/h; deadliest volcanic hazard.
Volcanic mudflow; melted ice + ash; killed 23000 at Armero (Nevado del Ruiz 1985).

walkthroughs.body_html: At constructive boundaries, partial melting of mantle produces basalt. At subduction zones, water-rich melts produce andesite to rhyolite. Higher silica means higher viscosity and more dissolved gas trapped, leading to explosive eruptions.

Kilauea Hawaii (continuous, VEI 0-1) vs Mt St Helens 1980 (VEI 5, 1.3 km^3 ejecta) vs Tambora 1815 (VEI 7, 160 km^3, year without summer). Yellowstone Lava Creek (640 ka, VEI 8) is largest known. Krakatoa 1883 (VEI 6) killed 36000 with tsunami.

VEI 4 eruption April-May 2010 from beneath Eyjafjallajokull ice cap produced fine ash plume to 9 km. Closure of European airspace cost airline industry $1.7 billion; 100000 flights cancelled affecting 10 million passengers. Few direct casualties but huge economic impact.
